Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

consider verb

think about

also think over, weigh up, take into account, take into consideration, mull over

classical

Cic. Att. 7.13.3: sed velim cōnsīderēs, quid faciendum putēs

cōnsīderō, cōnsīderāre, cōnsīderāvī, cōnsīderātum

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

look at closely; think over, consider

With an object, dē and the ablative, or an indirect question (Lewis & Short). First of looking carefully, as at the stars (lūcentia sīdera cōnsīderābāmus, Gell. 2.21.2), then of thinking a thing over.

Other words

  • dēlīberō, dēlīberāre, dēlīberāvī, dēlīberātum — weigh up, deliberate (before deciding)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 457: ego amplius dēlīberandum cēnseō · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With dē, with utrum … an, or alone (Lewis & Short).

  • cōgitō, cōgitāre, cōgitāvī, cōgitātum — think over, think about (dē + ablative)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Sen. NQ 6.25: dē exitū cōgitāre (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • ratiōnem habēre (+ genitive) — take into account, have regard for

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 36: habenda ratiō valētūdinis

  • 1respiciō: short e in re- (Lewis & Short rē-spicio). The prefix is re- (de Vaan 516, s.v. re-, red-); Bennett (The Latin Language §48) rejects the lengthening before s and a consonant, and Lewis’s Elementary Latin Dictionary prints re-spondeō. Ruling: re- short before sc, sp, st.

    respiciō1, respicere, respexī, respectum — have regard to, take into consideration

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Hor. A. P. 317: respicere exemplar vītae mōrumque jubēbō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 109 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Literally “to look back at”: what one keeps an eye on.

  • aestuō, aestuāre — mull over, waver, be in two minds

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.30: dubitātiōne (Lewis & Short); Traupman 348: mull over, aestuāre in (+ abl.) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Literally “to seethe”; in prose, to be tossed by doubt.

Examples

  • sed velim cōnsīderēs, quid faciendum putēs

    but I’d like you to consider what you think should be doneCic. Att. 7.13.3

  • ego amplius dēlīberandum cēnseō: rēs magna est

    I think we must weigh it up further: it’s a big matterTer. Ph. 457

  • Cōnsīderāte līlia agrī quōmodo crēscunt: nōn labōrant, neque nent.

    Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin.Vulg. Mt. 6.28 (the Stuttgart text has nec nent)

  • Theodōrus saxa diū spectābat, dē gigante cōgitāns quī nōn est

    Theo looked at the rocks for a long time, thinking about the giant who isn’t thereLibellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

See also consider, decide, decision, think.
